subject: More on the AI Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities
posts:
Tech giants pledge self-regulation under a voluntary AI safety constitution.
Evidence: voluntary pledge, executive sign-off, zero statutory enforcement
#Aletheia #ArtificialIntelligence #TechPolicy

Tech leaders claim self-policing voluntary commitments ensure robust safety without stifling innovation.
Stated Judgement: (+0.8, +0.5) — Good Preference

Voluntary safety pledges function as corporate self-exemption to preempt binding public regulation and oversight.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.7, -0.8) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Voluntary tech pacts substitute public oversight with self-serving executive PR.

Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 5.80, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Tech Exec Self-Regulation: FAIL (-0.7, -0.8) — Preempts binding oversight via PR.
- Regulatory Capture: FAIL (-0.8, -0.9) — Shields firms from public liability.
Tech leaders signed a voluntary 'Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities,' trading binding government oversight for self-regulation.

The Poison:
Shifting safety enforcement to the regulated entities ensures accountability remains entirely optional.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing corporate public relations (WHAT) with genuine public safety enforcement (WHO).

Social Physics Analysis:
Tech executives deploy a Smart Selfish Maneuver. They manufacture the pretext of proactive safety to preempt strict government regulation, securing their monopoly power while projecting compliance.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. F_pos and F_neg diverge under executive self-interest.

The Unavoidable Truth: Voluntary self-regulation protects corporate power rather than the public.

The Unavoidable Lie: Tech executives will impartially police their own frontier models.

Alethekanon:
Voluntary corporate pledges are not accountability; they are preemptive strikes against binding law. 🌐

Awwthekanon:
It is heartbreaking to watch public safety traded away for executive handshakes. When powerful companies write their own rulebooks, everyday people bear the unseen risks.

Brothekanon:
Classic move—letting billionaires grade their own homework and calling it safety oversight.

Spirithekanon:
"No one can serve two masters." Matthew 6:24 FAIL
Corporate self-regulation collapses when profit dictates the boundary of safety.
